video.title: Anthropic researchers are quitting... and now we know why

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Cold-open story. Hook: a 27-year-old researcher quit Anthropic before his shares vested; LinkedIn humblebrag contrast; payoff lands when he accuses OpenAI and Anthropic of 'gambling with our lives' (30.9). Ending after the colleague's 'yeah he's right' and the >10%-in-a-decade odds (46.5) also works -- a stronger kicker but a second beat -- so the end range genuinely spans both; shorter preferred.

Hacking group Shiny Hunters uses Claude to decompile 1.8M Android APKs and mine vibe-coded apps for hard-coded API keys; the irony that the keys they wanted most were Claude/OpenAI keys lands at 164.4, and the bit's punchline 'we need to put a stop to this Claude on Claude violence' at 174.9. Opens on 'But another hacking group that loves Claude' -- a light connective, but the line names the group and the premise, so no later start works.

Comedy bit. Hook: 'I'm an optimist, I'll bet a million dollars humanity won't be extinct in 10 years'; setup: humanity will instead be kept under 500 million per the Georgia Guidestones, 'obviously' instructions for ASI; punchline: somebody blew them up so ASI won't know what to do (279.5), button 'The bombing is under investigation' (281.7).

Yudkowsky's argument from 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies': a smarter system plays nice, passes evals, waits for us to build robots and bio labs, a brief utopia ('cure cancer, AIDS, and my herpes'), then the lights go out -- 'AI doesn't love you or hate you, you're just made of atoms it could use for something else' (315.1). The 'That's a terrifying idea, but AI hasn't killed us yet' line (319.1) is an acceptable button before the sponsor turn. Opening 'not nearly as optimistic as I am' reads fine without the previous bit.

also_ok.why: Two misuse examples from Anthropic's threat report: Midnight Blizzard's agents auto-rewrite flagged malware (babushka's basement joke), then two Chinese undergrads run an autonomous zero-day foundry. Surprising facts, but a list of examples without a single payoff; acceptable, not insisted on.

'The most horrendous use of Claude was distillation... which ironically Claude stole from books and bloggers', then DeepSeek/Alibaba/Moonshot accusations with numbers. Joke is up front; the rest is report detail, so an editor might take it but would not insist.

negatives.why: Intro ('In today's video', date, Code Report) into the list of seven misuse categories -- energetic but a table of contents.
Gain-of-function 'chicken chicken gonna kill you virus' and kill drones: a scary claim and a gag name, but two quick list items with no payoff; ~22s.
Footnote that distillation didn't run on Fable/Mythos so safeguards improve, then 'none matters if we're all dead in 10 years' -- depends on the distillation section and the cold open's 10-year odds.
Macroscope sponsor read, including the tempting 'either really good or those customers are fucked' joke.
